title: L11 · Lower Extremity
subtitle: Pelvic girdle, coxal bone, femur, tibia and fibula, ankle and foot

lines.text: Let's walk down the leg.
The two **coxal bones** form the pelvic girdle.
The **femur** is the thigh.
The **tibia** and **fibula** are the leg.
Then the **tarsals**, metatarsals and phalanges.
The **pelvic girdle** is two coxal bones.
The **pelvis** is four bones: both coxal bones, the sacrum and the coccyx.
Each coxal bone is three fused bones.
The **ilium**, the **ischium** and the **pubis**.
The **iliac crest** is the top ridge.
It ends in front at the **ASIS**, the anterior superior iliac spine.
The anterior inferior iliac spine is below it.
It ends in back at the **PSIS**, the posterior superior iliac spine.
The ilium meets the sacrum at the **SI joint**, the sacroiliac joint.
The iliac fossa is the inside wall of the basin.
The **greater sciatic notch** is a deep curve on the back.
Nerves, vessels and the **piriformis** muscle pass through it.
The **ischial spine** sits between the two sciatic notches.
The **ischial tuberosity** is the big rough bump you sit on.
The lesser sciatic notch is between them.
The pubic tubercles are small bumps on top of the pubis.
The two pubic bones meet at the **pubic symphysis**, a cartilage joint.
The **acetabulum** is the hip socket.
All three coxal bones fuse there.
It meets the femoral head at the hip joint.
The **obturator foramen** is the largest foramen in the body.
It's formed by the ischium and pubis. The eyes of the pelvis.
The femoral **head** points medially. The neck is just below it.
The **fovea capitis** is a pit in the head where a ligament attaches.
The **greater trochanter** is the big lateral bump.
The **lesser trochanter** is the small medial bump.
The **linea aspera** is a ridge down the back.
The medial and lateral **condyles** are smooth surfaces at the knee.
The epicondyles sit above them.
The **adductor tubercle** sits above the medial epicondyle.
The **patella** rides on the front. It's the largest sesamoid bone.
The tibia is the shin bone. It's large, medial and **weight bearing**.
Its condyles meet the femoral condyles.
The **tibial tuberosity** anchors the patellar ligament.
The **anterior crest** is the ridge of the shin.
The **medial malleolus** is the inner ankle bump.
The fibula is small, lateral and **non-weight bearing**.
The **fibular head** is at the top.
The **lateral malleolus** is the outer ankle bump.
An interosseous membrane joins the tibia and fibula.
Seven tarsals. Tiger Cubs Need MILC.
**Talus**, **calcaneus**, **navicular**, **cuboid**, and the medial, intermediate and lateral **cuneiforms**.
The calcaneus is the heel, the largest tarsal.
The talus sits on top. With the tibia and fibula it forms the talocrural joint, the true ankle.
The navicular is medial. The cuboid is lateral.
Five **metatarsals** form the arch. Number 1 is the big toe.
Each foot has 14 **phalanges**. Three per toe, two in the big toe.
